sections.title: Tech Neck Treatment in Downtown Austin

paras.t: Hours looking down at a laptop and a phone add up. Casey Morgan D.C. treats the neck and shoulder pain that comes with a desk job, a few minutes from downtown.

bullets.text: In and out in minutes, not rushed

sections.name: What Section
sections.title: If you work at a screen all day

paras.t: You notice it at 3pm. A tight neck, a knot between your shoulder blades, maybe a headache behind your eyes. You roll your shoulders, it helps for ten minutes, and then it's back.
That's tech neck. It's what years of looking down does to the top of your spine, and it's one of the most common things Dr. Morgan treats.

sections.name: What Section
sections.title: Your head is heavier than you think

paras.t: Your neck is built to hold your head balanced on top of it. Every inch your head drifts forward, the muscles in your neck and upper back work harder to hold it up.
Do that eight hours a day for a few years and the curve in your neck starts to straighten out. The muscles stay tight because they never get a break, and the joints stop moving the way they should.

callouts.title: A better chair alone won't undo it.
callouts.text: Ergonomics help keep it from getting worse. Getting the joints moving again is the part that fixes it.

sections.name: Header – Find it, fix it, keep it from coming bac
sections.title: Find it, fix it, keep it from coming back

paras.t: Built for your workday. Most visits after the first take a few minutes. You can come in on a lunch break and be back at your desk.

bullets.body: An exam of your neck and upper back, and digital X-rays on site when your exam calls for them, so you can see what years at a desk have done to the curve in your neck.
Chiropractic adjustments to get the neck and upper back moving again. Dr. Morgan starts gentle on the first visit.
Once it's corrected, most patients move to maintenance, about once every two weeks. If you're still at a desk eight hours a day, that's usually what keeps it from creeping back.

sections.name: First Visit Section
sections.title: Your first visit, start to finish

paras.t: First visit runs about 30 minutes. After that, most visits take a few minutes. Dr. Morgan built the practice around working people.

steps.title: We find out what is actually happening
steps.text: Full history and exam. What hurts, what you have already tried, what you want to get back to doing. Any necessary digital X-rays, taken on site.

steps.title: Dr. Morgan shows you the imaging, same day
steps.text: He marks it up and walks you through it right there. You will see what he sees. Most patients get their first adjustment the same visit.

steps.title: You come back for the full report
steps.text: Within a few days, Dr. Morgan lays out what he found and exactly what he recommends. What it will take, how long, and what it costs. Then you decide.

sections.name: What Section
sections.title: How long until this actually feels better

paras.t: Most people want a number before they start. Dr. Morgan will give you one, just not before he has examined you and looked at your imaging. He will not guess.
What he can tell you up front is how it usually goes, including the part most offices skip: the first two weeks are uneven.
If you are only trying to get out of pain, a shorter plan can do that. If you want it to stay fixed, it takes about 90 days. Dr. Morgan will give you both options and let you pick.

tags.text: Inconsistent, and that's normal. You'll have a good day and think it's fixed, then a bad one and think it's not working. Dr. Morgan warns you about this on day one. Real change usually starts around the end of week two, and better sleep is often the first thing people notice.

The bulk of the plan. A typical plan is about 24 visits over 90 days, two to three times a week at the start, then less often as you improve. Some people need fewer. Dr. Morgan checks your progress along the way.
Most patients move to maintenance, about once every two weeks. Some stop entirely. Dr. Morgan will tell you when you're there.

faqs.a: Neck and upper back pain from spending hours looking down at a computer or phone. The head drifts forward, the neck works harder to hold it up, and over time the joints and muscles pay for it.

faqs.q: Can a chiropractor fix tech neck?
faqs.a: When the problem is how your neck and upper back are moving, which it usually is, adjustments are what Dr. Morgan uses to get them moving again. The exam tells him whether that's what's going on.

faqs.q: Will a standing desk fix it?
faqs.a: It can help, and so can raising your screen to eye level. But if the joints have already stopped moving well, setup changes alone usually don't undo it.
